3.speaker: Petr Vectern
3.text: “Anton! Finally! Now the real party can start. Come on in!”

4.speaker: Player
4.text: “Thank you, Petr. What's next? A choir? A marching band?”

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Far from becoming accustomed to my workload as president, I only felt more and more snowed under as the weeks passed. It had been ages since I had any time to myself.
5.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_SmallMediumBusinesses"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_SmallMediumBusinesses"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_LargeCorporations"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_LargeCorporations"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_SmallMediumBusinesses"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_SmallMediumBusinesses"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromotePlanned"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromotePlanned"] == true) == false)

6.speaker: Player_Italic
6.text: Gesture at one of the waitresses to come over.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: I was starting to lose my focus, and my temper was growing increasingly thin. Petr was the first to realize I needed a break.
7.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Signed"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Signed"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false)

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: After much cajoling, he finally persuaded me to come to a meeting of his new venture: Gentlemen's Club.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: For the past few months, he'd been hosting a salon of sorts, not just for politicians and businessmen but also for artists, entertainers -- people of taste, he told me with a smile on his face.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: There was only one rule: no wives or girlfriends allowed. Hence the name.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: And so I found myself in front of his new luxury villa in Erlory. Very loud jazz music emanated from inside. I waited and waited. Finally Petr opened the door. I could smell the whiskey on his breath.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: We walked through the corridors of his mansion. Statues and paintings lined the stark white walls. An arched window provided a view of the neatly manicured grounds, complete with a swimming pool.

13.speaker: Petr Vectern
13.text: “Gentlemen! A minute of your time please.”

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: As soon as I entered, Petr closed the door and turned to the small crowd.

15.speaker: Petr Vectern
15.text: “I now have the privilege to present to you... The man himself... The fourth President of Sordland, Mr. Anton Rayne!”

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: I'd known him for long enough to understand that he was more than a little drunk. He made an elaborate mock-curtsy as I passed him and walked into the room. The music stopped, and I felt everyone's eyes on me.

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “And I present to you, Petr Vectern. The first alcoholic Vice President of Sordland.”

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: My joke didn't sit well with Petr, nor the crowd. There was a short awkward silence before he continued.

20.speaker: Petr Vectern
20.text: “No. I'm saving those for your funeral."

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: Petr laughed very hard at his own grim joke before continuing.

22.speaker: Petr Vectern
22.text: “Dear members, please give a warm welcome to our very special guest! If I may, Anton. Here, take this.”

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: He handed me a glass of whiskey and put his hand on my shoulder.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: Petr nodded at me and turned to the attendees.

26.speaker: Petr Vectern
26.text: “Anton Rayne might have the power to make presidential decrees, but, I, Petr Vectern, the president of this club, now declare this party started! Music! Go!"

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: After greeting the crowd around me, I felt a hand on my shoulder.

29.speaker: Petr Vectern
29.text: “That chandelier was made in the 18th century. Can you believe it? There's even a hedge maze in the garden!”

31.speaker: Player
31.text: “How are you paying for all of this?”

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “An 18th-century chandelier? A hedge maze? A little much, isn't it?”

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: A grand Lespian marble staircase led up to the second story. Petr gestured at the massive crystal chandelier hanging overhead.

34.speaker: Petr Vectern
34.text: “I don't know and I don't care. It just looks expensive and I like it.”

35.speaker: Petr Vectern
35.text: “I'll let you in on a secret. Gus Manger has a lot of contacts in real estate. He brokered an amazing price for me.”

36.speaker: Petr Vectern
36.text: “Ah, come on, Anton. You only live once.”

37.speaker: Petr Vectern
37.text: “He'll also be here tonight, by the way."

38.speaker: Player
38.text: "What did you promise him in return?"

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “Perfect. I've been looking for a chance to speak with him about investment opportunities."

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: We continued walking until we circled back to where we had started.

42.speaker: Petr Vectern
42.text: “So, what do you think of my little hideaway?”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Living in a lavish mansion while my country suffers is not for me.”

45.speaker: Petr Vectern
45.text: “I understand completely. That's why I've donated 30 percent of my vice presidential salary to charities."

47.speaker: Player
47.text: “It's amazing, but I'd hardly call it a hideaway. More like a palace.”

48.speaker: Petr Vectern
48.text: “Jealous, are we? Like I said, you could have a place just like this.”

50.speaker: Petr Vectern
50.text: “Thanks! You know that you, Monica and the kids are always welcome here.”

51.speaker: Petr Vectern
51.text: “Anyway, let's get back to the party.”

52.speaker: Petr Vectern
52.text: “I arranged for some caviar to be brought in from Lespia. You're going to love it.”

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: He opened the door to the main hall, and we rejoined the other guests. The music was louder now, and the mood decidedly more inebriated.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: Cocktail waitresses were carrying around plates of canapés, wearing dresses that left little to the imagination.

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: She was in her mid-twenties, wearing red lipstick, her blonde hair neatly tied into a ponytail. On her plate were toast points slathered in the Lespian caviar Petr had mentioned.

57.speaker: Player
57.text: “So this is what you've been hiding from Evelyn.”

58.speaker: Petr Vectern
58.text: “Lespian caviar, best in the world! I'm telling you, Anton, there are few pleasures in life that are this..."

59.speaker: Petr Vectern
59.text: “No one is hiding anything. She knows how important it is for men like us to blow off steam once in a while."

60.speaker: Narrator
60.text: He averted his gaze for a second before calling over one of the waitresses.

61.speaker: Petr Vectern
61.text: “Would you rather get served by wrinkly old men? Sweetheart! Over here!”

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: He waved at one of the waitresses, and she came over to us.

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: As the waitress left us to serve another attendee, she flashed a quick smile at Petr over her shoulder. He smiled back, a little too broadly.

64.speaker: Petr Vectern
64.text: “Oh look, there's Gus. Why don't you go talk to him? I'll be back in a minute.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “Petr. I am warning you. Don't make a mistake.”

67.speaker: Petr Vectern
67.text: “Mistake? What are you talking about? I'm just going to the... washroom. See you shortly."

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: He left the room and I headed over to Gus.

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: Gus Manger was standing next to a couple of men that I recognized as banking industry magnates. As I approached, all of them turned to me and bowed their heads.

70.speaker: Gus Manger
70.text: “Mr. President. A toast to our new member, everyone!”

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: Gus and I clinked our glasses as the people around us raised theirs.

72.speaker: Player
72.text: “You don't seem at all surprised to see me here.”

73.speaker: Player
73.text: “How long have you been a member?”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “I heard this mansion is a result of your connections.”

75.speaker: Gus Manger
75.text: “That's right. I do have a wide network in real estate.”

76.speaker: Petr Vectern
76.text: “We all know why we're gathered here tonight. To celebrate life. To have a brief escape from our tumultuous professions.”

77.speaker: Petr Vectern
77.text: “I personally don't know any better cure for stress than a little drink.”

78.speaker: Petr Vectern
78.text: “Now. The tradition dictates that as the club president, I have to remind you of our house rules. There are three. No politics. No wives. No one sober! Cheers!”

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: Petr drank the whiskey in his glass in one go.

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: A few people in the crowd chuckled and some raised their glasses.

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: People in the crowd laughed and raised their glasses.

87.speaker: Gus Manger
87.text: “Since the beginning. It's a fun gathering, and quite lucrative at times."

88.speaker: Gus Manger
88.text: “That's because Petr told me you were going to come.”

89.speaker: Gus Manger
89.text: “He also told me that you might be interested in potential opportunities such as, well... this."

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: He opened his arms, gesturing at our opulent surroundings.

91.speaker: Gus Manger
91.text: “You might've heard from Petr that I arranged the deal for this mansion.”

92.speaker: Gus Manger
92.text: “Petr told me a couple of weeks ago that you might be interested in potential opportunities such as, well... this.”

93.speaker: Gus Manger
93.text: “Let's take a walk. The balcony has an amazing view of Erlory.”

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: We left the room and made our way to the balcony. On the way, he took out two cigars and held one out for me.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: We went out to the balcony. All of Erlory was at our feet. From this vantage point, I was able to see how expansive the building plot was. The swimming pool and the hedge maze were visible from here.

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: Leaning over the railing, I admired the view for a moment before Gus spoke up.

99.speaker: Gus Manger
99.text: “Real estate is the best investment anyone can make. With the current economic situation, it only makes sense to put your money into such a tangible asset."

100.speaker: Gus Manger
100.text: “But I also have a few other opportunities for you to make a side profit, if real estate doesn't interest you."

101.speaker: Gus Manger
101.text: “Is there any chance I can convince you?”

102.speaker: Gus Manger
102.text: “I would be delighted to discuss a similar arrangement with you. In fact, I have prepared a document with my own personal favorite opportunities.”
102.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_CompanyFulfilled"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Embargo_Arcasia"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true

103.speaker: Petr Vectern
103.text: “He'll have a once-in-a-lifetime deal ready for you. He always does."

105.speaker: Petr Vectern
105.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_CompanyFulfilled"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Embargo_Arcasia"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true

106.speaker: Petr Vectern
106.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_CompanyFulfilled"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Embargo_Arcasia"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true) == false

107.speaker: Gus Manger
107.text: “I would have been delighted to work with you, but unfortunately a deal won't be possible at this time. Not from me or my contacts at least.”

108.speaker: Gus Manger
108.text: “The Gasom affair notwithstanding, you've shown plenty of generosity to Sordish businesses. You deserve a chance to profit personally from their gains.”

111.speaker: Gus Manger
111.text: “There have been some issues with my business, Mr. Rayne. Nothing life-or-death. But the hard work I put on the cancelled railway took up so much of my time that I've had to postpone some projects. I'm sure you understand.”

115.speaker: Gus Manger
115.text: “I have already made my investment. Unfortunately, I have yet to see a return."

116.speaker: Gus Manger
116.text: “I know you're wondering about the deal Petr made. In a nutshell, thanks to my network he was able to procure this house for half the asking price, which would've been impossible under any other circumstances.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “I'm glad my investment decisions are paying off.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “I am not looking to make any investments at the moment.”

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “All right. Let me see what you have available.”

130.speaker: Gus Manger
130.text: “If you'll excuse me now, I will go refresh my drink. See you around.”

132.speaker: Gus Manger
132.text: “Nothing, Mr. President. It's a simple thank you for supporting me.”

133.speaker: Gus Manger
133.text: “If you'll excuse me, I'm going to refresh my drink. See you around.”

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: Gus opened his briefcase and pulled out a thin dossier. He showed it to me.

135.speaker: Gus Manger
135.text: "There's also the option of a football partnership. I already own a large portion of FC Anrica, and I'm doing my best to make them champions. Buying in would be more expensive than the vineyard, but this season will bring a lot of returns, I'm quite positive."

136.speaker: Gus Manger
136.text: “My biggest opportunity, though, is the possibility to buy shares in Underhall Construction. My connections ensured me that this would not be open to the public and would benefit you greatly. As you know, they are the biggest construction company in Sordland...”

137.speaker: Gus Manger
137.text: "My first offer is, of course, real estate. There is a vineyard close to Erlory, about a one-hour drive from here, that also includes a very large villa. A beautiful plot, but rather neglected, so there would be a fair amount of renovation costs. On the bright side, you would be able to produce your own wine. The previous owner was Giralt of Ribery, a world-renowned vintner."

138.speaker: Gus Manger
138.text: “Give me the word, and I will start the procurement process. But we must act quickly as these options might soon disappear off the market.”
138.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Faction_Oligarchs_Content"] == true) == false

139.speaker: Player
139.text: “Football sounds exciting. I'll invest in FC Anrica.” [-2 Personal Wealth]

140.speaker: Player
140.text: “I'll invest in Underhall Construction.” [-2 Personal Wealth]
140.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.PersonalWealth"] > 1) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Faction_Oligarchs_Content"] == true)

141.speaker: Player
141.text: “The vineyard in Erlory. I've always wanted to have my own wine. And it sounds peaceful and quiet.” [-1 Personal Wealth]

142.speaker: Player
142.text: “On second thought, I don't want to do this now.”

143.speaker: Gus Manger
143.text: “Very well. Do not blame me if they are not available at a later date.”

147.speaker: Gus Manger
147.text: “Excellent. I will start the process right away. Now if you'll excuse me, Mr. President.”

148.speaker: Gus Manger
148.text: “If you'll excuse me, I'm going to refresh my drink. See you around.”

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: He left to rejoin the party. Alone on the balcony, I looked out over Erlory.

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: Suddenly, I heard a rustling from the hedge maze below.

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: I looked down and saw a silhouette. Two silhouettes, actually, so close together they seemed to be entangled. I squinted and tried to get a better look. It was definitely two people kissing, but I couldn't see either of their faces.

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: I returned to the party and spent some time mingling with the other guests, engaging them in small talk about their businesses, their children, their relationships.

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: Just then, Petr came up from behind us and threw an arm around each of our shoulders.

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: He poured us two large glasses of whiskey, and we drank them in one go. Throughout the party, we drank and drank. Just like old times.

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: I woke up the next day with a pounding headache and more than a few regrets.

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: My recollections of the evening were hazy, but there was one important detail that kept coming back to me.

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: The red lipstick on Petr's collar.

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: But maybe my memory was playing tricks on me.

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: I took a bite. It was rich, salty, tasting of pure seaside. I could almost hear the sound of waves and seagulls.

167.speaker: Petr Vectern
167.text: “Anton! Finally! Come in, relax, take a break from this crisis!”

168.speaker: Player
168.text: “I'd like to make a similarly profitable arrangement myself.”
168.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_CompanyFulfilled"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Embargo_Arcasia"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true) == false

169.speaker: Player
169.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_CompanyFulfilled"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Embargo_Arcasia"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true) == false

170.speaker: Player
170.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Walter_Promise_CompanyFulfilled"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Embargo_Arcasia"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == true) == false

172.speaker: Player
172.text: “I don't think I can afford an investment right now.”

176.speaker: Petr Vectern
176.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Faction_Oligarchs_Content"] == true) == false

179.speaker: Petr Vectern
179.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Faction_Oligarchs_Content"] == true) == false

221.speaker: Petr Vectern
221.text: “That's what it says on my tax forms, at least.”

223.speaker: Narrator
223.text: His eyes were still fixed on her, with an expression I remembered from our many nights out together as students.

224.speaker: Petr Vectern
224.text: "Oh, just to the washroom. See you shortly."

243.speaker: Gus Manger
243.text: “There have been some issues with my business, Mr. Rayne. Nothing life-or-death. But I've been putting so much work into advancing rural development that I've had to postpone some projects. I'm sure you understand.”

262.speaker: Gus Manger
262.text: "You must know that the offered price is not suitable for every client.”

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "Why am I not surprised? Gus the wheeler and dealer would be right at home at a party like this."

270.speaker: Petr Vectern
270.text: "Hell, half of the guests here owe their considerable riches to him."

274.speaker: Gus Manger
274.text: “Your willingness to invest in Gasom showed you were a man after my own heart. I'd love to talk about how my network can benefit you personally."

275.speaker: Narrator
275.text: I realized it had been a while since Petr left. I looked around, but couldn't find him. Instead, my eyes landed on Ewald Alphonso.

277.speaker: Narrator
277.text: With a reluctant look in his eyes, the former president walked over to meet me.

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: With a smile, the former president walked over to meet me.

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "Mr. Alphonso. I didn't know you were a member of Petr's club."

283.speaker: Player
283.text: "Mr. President. Is that an empty glass I see in your hand?"

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "Isn't a party like this a little low-class for a man like you?"

286.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
286.text: "I'm not. Gus and I were having a business dinner, and he convinced me to come along afterwards."

287.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
287.text: "The surroundings are a little tacky, I admit. But Gus convinced me the networking opportunities would be unparalleled."

288.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
288.text: "I saw you speaking to Mr. Manger earlier."

289.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
289.text: "I'm trying to pace myself. Gus and I split a bottle of Rizian wine over dinner before heading here."

290.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
290.text: "No politics. But plenty of side deals, it seems."

294.speaker: Player
294.text: "That's right. He offered me some lucrative investment opportunities."

295.speaker: Player
295.text: "Yes, he and I are going into business together."

296.speaker: Player
296.text: "Just briefly. I wasn't interested in what he was offering."

297.speaker: Player
297.text: "He seems used to making deals with sitting presidents. But he and I won't be going into business."

298.speaker: Player
298.text: "We talked, yes. It's always nice to get to know one's ministers outside of the Maroon Palace."

302.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
302.text: "Hmm. Interesting that you'd take him up on that while ignoring the far more lucrative opportunity to invest in Gasom."

303.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
303.text: "Why not? Seems like a natural progression after our Gasom deal."

307.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
307.text: "Although your tightening of the Energy Protection Act shows your carelessness with that particular investment."

311.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
311.text: "Although your tightening of the Energy Protection Act -- despite your promise to me -- shows your carelessness with that particular investment."

315.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
315.text: "Although your tightening of the Energy Protection Act proves that a profitable Gasom was never your goal."

319.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
319.text: "Although your tightening of the Energy Protection Act -- despite your promise to me -- proves that a profitable Gasom was never your goal."

320.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
320.text: "At any rate, it's doing fine without Sordland's input. A shame that only its international investors will benefit."

321.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
321.text: "We're seeing growing interest from international investors, by the way. I'm optimistic about the results of Sordland's investment."

325.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
325.text: "It figures. I don't know why he thought you'd be interested in other investments after you passed on the Gasom opportunity."

326.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
326.text: "Interesting. I would have thought you'd be interested in other opportunities after investing in Gasom."

327.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
327.text: "We had a good chat together back in Narbel, as I recall."

331.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
331.text: "Before you turned down the opportunity to invest in Gasom, that is."

332.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
332.text: "Resulting in your very wise decision to invest Sordish money in Gasom."

334.speaker: Player
334.text: "Terrific. I'm looking forward to a big payoff."

335.speaker: Player
335.text: "I'm glad that Sordland could help your company thrive."

336.speaker: Player
336.text: "Enjoy our bailout, Mr. Alphonso. It'll be your only one."

338.speaker: Player
338.text: "I still stand by my decision. There were better uses for that money."

339.speaker: Player
339.text: "Yes, perhaps Sordland should've invested. But it's too late for regrets."

340.speaker: Player
340.text: "I'm sorry about that. My party forced me to do it."

341.speaker: Player
341.text: "Unlike you, I know better than to mess with a successful Tarquin Soll policy."

342.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
342.text: "I know how much pressure the USP can exert. But I also know that with a little courage, resistance is possible."

343.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
343.text: "It seems your courage failed you. And you, in turn, have failed Gasom."

344.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
344.text: "That policy put a chokehold on Sordish businesses. Thanks to you, it is doing so again."

346.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
346.text: "Better uses, maybe. But not more profitable ones."

347.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
347.text: "It's not too late to remember to take more risks in the future."

349.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
349.text: "No politics. But this conversation is not over."

350.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
350.text: "As I've told you, this isn't a bailout. You'll get your money back and then some."

352.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
352.text: "I can't tell you for sure how big it will be. But our projections are looking good."

353.speaker: Petr Vectern
353.text: "Look at you two! Sordland's bright future and its ancient, ancient past."

355.speaker: Player
355.text: "It's been an hour. Where were you?"

356.speaker: Player
356.text: "My apologies, Mr. Alphonso. My vice president's had a bit too much to drink."

358.speaker: Petr Vectern
358.text: "I told you. The washroom. Trust me, you'd rather not know the details."

360.speaker: Petr Vectern
360.text: "Pardon me, Mr. President, but I've had exactly enough."

361.speaker: Petr Vectern
361.text: "Yes, Mr. President. Right away, Mr. President."

362.speaker: Petr Vectern
362.text: "Well, Mr. Alphonso? Have you been enjoying my hospitality?"

364.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
364.text: "Indeed I have, Mr. Vectern. You've put together one hell of a gathering."

365.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
365.text: "If you'll excuse me, I'm going to have a quick word with the CEO of Sordish Petroleum."

367.speaker: Player
367.text: "Have fun mingling. It was good to see you."

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: Alphonso gave a brusque wave and walked off.

375.speaker: Petr Vectern
375.text: "Nice guy. I almost feel bad about the way we took him down."

376.speaker: Petr Vectern
376.text: "Nice guy. A shitty president, but a nice guy."

377.speaker: Player
377.text: "Was that you in the hedge maze, Petr?"

378.speaker: Player
378.text: "Why didn't you tell me Ewald Alphonso was coming?"

379.speaker: Player
379.text: "I will give you one more chance. Where were you?"

380.speaker: Petr Vectern
380.text: "I didn't know! Gus brought him along. And when a former president of Sordland knocks on your door, you can't exactly turn him away."

382.speaker: Petr Vectern
382.text: "Well, Mr. President, when too much Sordish whiskey meets too much Lespian caviar, it can lead to a gastrointestinal imbroglio the likes of which the world has never seen."

384.speaker: Player
384.text: "While you were gone, I saw two people kissing in the hedge maze outside."

385.speaker: Player
385.text: "I'll be direct. Were you with the waitress?"

386.speaker: Player
386.text: "You know what? Never mind. Let's get another drink."

387.speaker: Player
387.text: "Next time, I want to be able to vet your guest list. You're risking a breach of national security with these parties."

388.speaker: Player
388.text: "It's fine. I was happy to see him. But it was definitely a surprise."

389.speaker: Petr Vectern
389.text: "Anton. Can't a man have some fun outside of work?"

391.speaker: Petr Vectern
391.text: "That's what I'm aiming for with these parties. All kinds of unexpected, stimulating encounters."

392.speaker: Petr Vectern
392.text: "What? No, no. How could you even think that? I'm a married man."

393.speaker: Petr Vectern
393.text: "Huh. Probably a couple of kitchen staff getting frisky with each other. What do I even pay them for?"

395.speaker: Player
395.text: "Petr. You know you can tell me anything."

396.speaker: Petr Vectern
396.text: "But sure. If it'll make you happy, I'll tighten my villa's border control policy."

397.speaker: Narrator
397.text: He contorted the side of his face in an attempt at a wink.

398.speaker: Petr Vectern
398.text: "Now who wants a drink? Besides me, of course."

399.speaker: Narrator
399.text: I thought I saw his cheerful expression slip for a moment.

400.speaker: Petr Vectern
400.text: "Yeah. I know. Trust me, it's nothing."

405.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
405.text: "No politics. But your returns are not looking good, to say the least."
